name: Squash, Shiitake, Kale, and Kimchi Stew

ingredients.name: squash, ends trimmed, cut into 1/2-inch cubes
shiitake mushrooms, ends removed, caps sliced
kale, ends trimmed, leaves roughly chopped

instructions.primary_message: Warm sesame oil into a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Add scallion whites and garlic and cook, stirring occasionally, until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add squash and shiitakes, stir well, and cook until squash starts to soften, 3 to 5 minutes minutes. Add chopped kale and cook, stirring often, until leaves turn bright green and wilt slightly, about 2 minutes.

Stir in kimchi, kimchi liquid, stock, water, soy sauce, mirin, gochujang, and doenjang. Bring to a boil over high heat, reduce heat to a strong simmer. Stir in soft tofu and kochukaru (if using), and cook until kale is tender and soup has slightly thickened, about 10 minutes. Season to taste with more salt and chili flakes if desired.
Serve soup immediately, sprinkled with scallion greens.

schema_metadata.keywords: easy, kale, kimchi, quick, shiitake, soup, squash, tofu

description: I don't know about you, but kimchi stew (jjigae) reminds me of winter. But it turns out summer vegetables are equally at home in this dish. Plus, haven't you heard that adage that you should eat a hot soup on a hot day?
notes:
Optional or for serving: 2 tablespoons gochugaru (Korean dried chili flakes), more or less to taste (optional)

Optional substitutions: low-sodium vegetable broth → chicken broth; doenjang white miso paste → Japanese white miso paste
author: Nick Kindelsperger
